chunks: It is said that he lived for one hundred and twenty years, and no tooth or molar fell from his mouth. Some said: I saw him when he had reached eighty, and his teeth were being carried off (as if by a procession). Whenever a canine tooth fell out for him, another grew in its place. He was among the best of people in terms of teeth.
ai.seo_question: What was the unique dental characteristic of Nabigha al-Ju'di regarding his longevity?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights Nabigha al-Ju'di’s exceptional longevity, noting he lived 120 years with his teeth intact, a trait often cited in Islamic historiography as a sign of divine favor or unique physiological constitution. The detail of immediate tooth regeneration underscores the miraculous nature of his physical preservation, reflecting the broader Shia scholarly interest in extraordinary human attributes as indicators of spiritual or historical significance.
